The first-layer weights are dominated by channel 0 (agent) and channel 1 (moving objects). Channel 0 has large weights at many inner cells, especially lower-middle positions such as (r6,c3), (r6,c4), (r6,c5), (r7,c3), (r7,c4), (r7,c5), (r8,c5), and also some upper cells like (r2,c4), (r2,c5), (r3,c4), (r4,c5). This suggests the policy is tracking the agentâs position relative to other objects. Channel 1 has strong, scattered weights at distinct cells such as (r6,c8), (r6,c4), (r3,c6), (r3,c2), (r6,c6), (r6,c2), (r3,c7), (r3,c3), (r5,c2), (r5,c6). These look like several separate movable objects, not a single contiguous body. Channel 2 (reward targets) does not appear in any top-8 connection; its weights are all small. Channel 3 (obstacles) also does not appear in any top-8 connection; only the border walls exist, so the agent can avoid them from its own position. Channel 4 (previous frame) has large weights at cells like (r4,c7), (r5,c2), (r3,c8), (r3,c1), (r5,c8), (r5,c3), (r5,c7), (r4,c2), (r4,c6), (r5,c4), (r8,c4), which are useful for detecting recent movement of the agent or the movable objects. For example, unit 12 has (r5,c5,ch0) â8.723, (r3,c6,ch1) 6.689, (r3,c2,ch1) 6.639; unit 4 has (r5,c2,ch4) 6.182; unit 16 has (r4,c7,ch4) 6.440; unit 18 has (r3,c1,ch4) â4.351 and (r5,c8,ch4) â4.103. The output layer is omitted, but the 5 actions are no-op, up, down, left, right.

Reasoning:  
The network heavily uses the agentâs position and the positions of several movable objects, plus previous-frame information to infer movement. It almost completely ignores the reward-target channel and the obstacle channel. This fits a game where the reward targets are fixed and known, so the policy does not need to read them, and where the only obstacles are the fixed border walls. The movable objects are separate and can be pushed or moved by the agent. Sokoban matches this exactly: the agent pushes boxes (moving objects) onto fixed target squares; walls are mostly just the border; reward is given when boxes are on targets. Snake is ruled out because food is a random reward target and would require large channel-2 weights. Pac-Man is ruled out because pellets and internal walls would appear in channels 2 and 3. Simple maze tasks are ruled out because there are multiple moving objects. Pong is ruled out by the 5-action grid setup.

Game: Sokoban (likely a fixed 10Ã10 level).

Description: The agent controls a player in a grid and pushes boxes onto target squares. Reward is given when boxes are placed on targets, and the level is solved when all boxes are on targets.

Confidence: 90%
